name: Dockside Cold-Store Handler's Layered Full Kit
description: Workers managing cold-storage freight at Meridian Harbor's interior docking bays — pulling cryogenic cargo containers, operating pallet movers in sub-zero holds, stacking refrigerated units — dress for the cold first and everything else second. The base is a full-body thermal underlayer in pale grey moisture-wicking synth-fleece, close-fitting with flat seams to prevent pressure points under the outer gear, and a reinforced collar that can be pulled up over the lower face. Over this goes an insulated bib-overall in burnt orange — the standard color for cold-store certified workers — made from a quilted synth-nylon shell with hollow-fiber fill, rated to minus twenty Celsius. The bib straps are wide and padded, adjustable with quick-release buckles, and the side panels have stretch inserts for movement. A matching insulated work jacket in the same burnt orange goes over the bibs, with a sherpa-lined collar that folds up into a partial hood, heavy-duty glove loops on the cuffs, and a left-chest panel embroidered with the worker's facility number and a cold-store certification badge in reflective thread. Gauntlet-style insulated work gloves in black synth-leather with grip-dot palms hang from the cuff loops when not in use. The boots are wide-last insulated waterproof work boots with a composite safety toe, rated for cold-store floors, with oil and slip resistant soles. A thermal balaclava in grey synth-fleece covers the head and neck, leaving only the eyes clear, over which workers often clip a polycarbonate face shield on a bump cap.
functionality: Rated to minus twenty Celsius, full-body insulation layering system, quick-release bib buckles for emergency removal, grip-dot gloves for cryogenic container handling, slip-resistant cold-floor rated soles, face shield for cryo vapor exposure, reflective certification badge for hazard-zone identification, moisture-wicking base prevents sweat freeze
what_it_says: Certified cold-store. The burnt orange marks them as cleared for cryo-freight handling — not everyone on the dock floor has this certification, and the workers wearing it know it. There's a quiet pride in the insulated kit: it's better gear than most of the dock, it means the employer trusts you with the expensive cargo, and the certification badge is a real credential that transfers.
manufacturer: Meridian Harbor Authority (bib-overall and jacket, facility-issued); base layer by Ironpass; boots by Dockmaster supply contract
price_range: Φ220–Φ320 full kit (facility-subsidized; worker cost Φ60–Φ100)
story_hooks: A cold-store handler discovers a cryogenic unit in their assigned bay that isn't on the manifest — the internal temperature log shows it's been cycling for eleven days, and the container is locked to a biometric key that belongs to a harbor administrator who died three months ago.

The burnt orange cold-store certification color has been counterfeited — someone is moving through the harbor interior bays in fake-colored gear without clearance, and the real crew have started noticing a face they don't recognize on shift.

A new cold-store certification requirement is being rolled out that includes a mandatory BCI compliance chip embedded in the badge — workers who refuse the update lose their cold-store clearance, and a quiet work action is building on the dock floor.
